references.text: The Samaritan woman had just said that she knew the Messiah was coming ([ref:Joh 4:25|John 4:25]). Jesus' answer in verse 26 is a direct response to this messianic expectation – he reveals himself as the promised Messiah.

Jesus uses the solemn "Ἐγώ εἰμι" (I am) as a self-revelation. In [ref:Joh 8:24|John 8:24] he uses the same expression and links it to faith and salvation: "if you do not believe that I am, you will die in your sins".
In [ref:Joh 8:28|John 8:28] Jesus again says "I am" (Ἐγώ εἰμι) and points forward to the cross as the place where his identity will be fully revealed.
The great "I am" statement in [ref:Joh 8:58|John 8:58] ("Before Abraham was, I am") shows the deep divine self-identification that also lies behind Jesus' words to the Samaritan woman.
In [ref:Joh 18:5-6|John 18:5-6] Jesus says "I am he" (ἐγώ εἰμι) to those who came to arrest him, and they fell to the ground – a parallel use of the divine self-revelation.
God's self-revelation to Moses: "I am who I am" ([ref:2 Mos 3:14|Exodus 3:14]) forms the background for Jesus' "Ἐγώ εἰμι" statements, where he identifies himself with God's own name.
In [ref:Jes 43:10|Isaiah 43:10] the Lord says: "I am he" (אֲנִי הוּא). This divine self-testimony underlies Jesus' use of "I am" as a revelation of his divine identity.

In [ref:Jes 52:6|Isaiah 52:6] the Lord promises that the people will know his name and know "that it is I who speak" (אֲנִי־הוּא הַמְדַבֵּר). Jesus' words "I am, the one speaking to you" (ὁ λαλῶν σοι) have a striking parallel to this prophetic word.

In [ref:Joh 9:37|John 9:37] Jesus reveals himself to the man born blind with similar words: "You have seen him, and it is he who speaks to you." The structure of self-revelation through conversation is the same as in John 4:26.

In [ref:Mark 14:61-62|Mark 14:61-62] the high priest asks if Jesus is the Messiah, and Jesus answers "I am" (ἐγώ εἰμι). This is the most direct parallel to John 4:26, where Jesus in the same way confirms his identity as the Messiah.

Moses promised that the Lord would send a prophet like him ([ref:5 Mos 18:15-18|Deuteronomy 18:15-18]). The Samaritans were waiting for this prophetic figure (Taheb), and Jesus' self-revelation as the Messiah in John 4:26 fulfills this promise.
